page: Microsoft Azure D8s_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DSv4 server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor based on the x86_64 architecture, running at a clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The instance features 8 dedicated virtual CPUs, mapped from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes 32 KB of L1D cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of L3 cache, with support for advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AES cryptography. This instance does not include any local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable for external disk attachments.

Benchmark evaluations place the D8s_v4 in the average performance tier for most general-purpose workloads. It achieves a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1411.98 and a multi-core score of 7435.42. Memory bandwidth is measured at 414.43 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 44.87 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 32.6 GB/sec for large-block writes. In application-specific tests, the server demonstrates moderate capabilities, delivering 6.84 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 6.85 GB/sec of static web serving throughput. However, it exhibits weaker performance in single-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench single-core execution.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D8s_v4 offers a balanced resource profile suitable for standard enterprise workloads without the premium cost of specialized compute or memory-optimized hardware. The lack of bundled local storage means storage costs are decoupled, allowing users to scale Premium Storage independently. Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and solid multi-core performance, this server is well-suited for general-purpose applications, including static web serving, software compilation, database operations, and moderate text or image processing tasks.
